Subject: Acme discovery: latency/throughput follow-up and benchmarks

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the agreed next steps:

What we covered
- Your priority: minimize P50 latency for short-response generation (under 100 tokens) while keeping cost predictable.
- Workload: bursty web requests, ~25 RPS target for a single service, typical prompt length ~60 tokens.
- Questions you had: measured latencies at target RPS, throughput scaling, and whether prefix/KV caching fits your prompt chaining pattern.

Answers / artifacts attached
- Attached: redwood-latency-benchmarks.pdf (executed on g5x2-like hardware) and benchmark-summary.csv with run parameters.
- Short answer on latency: in our internal runs we see P50 ~60ms at sustained 25 RPS for a 60-token response using our optimized runtime with 4-bit quantization and request-level batching disabled. P95 was ~140ms under the same config.
- Caching: our KV/prefix caching works with chained prompts (we preserve KV across short session windows to avoid re-decoding past context). That should help you with repetitive prompt prefixes.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (30 min) with your infra team — Lukas (cc) can run through the benchmark config and answer kernel/hardware questions.
2) If timing looks good, a short PoC: we can stand up a dedicated eval route for you for 2–4 weeks to collect real traffic numbers.

Availability: Lukas and I are available next Tue/Wed afternoon (PST) or Fri morning. If those don't work, send a couple times that do.

Thanks — attached the runs and a one-pager. Happy to jump on a call and walk through any of the numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Appreciate the fast follow-up and the artifacts. A couple quick clarifying questions from our infra lead before we lock a deep-dive:

1) Can you confirm P50 ~60ms measurement was at payload size ~60 tokens and single-request latency (no large batching)?
2) How does that number change if we enable small (2–4) micro-batches to improve throughput during short bursts?
3) Are the runs single-instance numbers or aggregated across a pool — our goal is to size instances so we can hit 25 RPS without autoscaling.

If you can call out the config in the report (hardware, model variant, quantization) that'd help. I shared the files with our infra alias (infra@acme.com) — we may want Lukas to talk directly to our infra folks.

We're interested in a PoC but want to make sure the single-instance sizing is reasonable.

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
samir.patel@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme discovery: latency/throughput follow-up and benchmarks

Samir —

Thanks for the questions. Short, direct answers inline and a quick config summary below. Full details are in the attached acme-technical-answers.md and the CSV run outputs.

1) P50 context: yes — the ~60ms P50 was for a 60-token response, single-request latency (we disabled large batching for that run to prioritize tail behavior).
2) Micro-batching effect: introducing micro-batches of 2–4 increases throughput at the expense of P50. In our tests, 2-way batching raised P50 to ~80–85ms but improved sustained throughput by ~25%. If your traffic is bursty, a small micro-batch can be a good trade-off.
3) Instance sizing: numbers reported are per-instance (single serving process) on g5x2-equivalent hardware with our optimized kernels and 4-bit quantization. To hit 25 RPS at the P50 numbers above we recommend a single dedicated instance with the config in the attached runbook; if you prefer headroom, two instances provide better stability under burst.

Suggested next step: schedule a 30-min technical session where Lukas can walk through the run parameters (kernel selection, KV cache settings, batching policy) with your infra team. Proposed slots:
- Tue 10 Mar, 10:00–10:30 PST
- Wed 11 Mar, 14:00–14:30 PST

If you want, we can also spin up a short PoC route and replay a slice of your traffic to show real numbers — typically 1–2 weeks.

Let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: acme-technical-answers.md]
